method_card.title: Family Members and Relationships
method_card.content:
This lesson covers family member vocabulary, possessive adjectives, and relationship status in German.

GermanEnglish
der Vaterfather
die Muttermother
der Bruderbrother
die Schwestersister
die Eltern (pl.)parents
die Geschwister (pl.)siblings
der Opa / die Omagrandpa / grandma
der Onkel / die Tanteuncle / aunt
der Stiefvaterstepfather
das Einzelkindonly child
verheiratetmarried
geschiedendivorced

Grammar focus: Possessive adjectives (mein, dein, sein, ihr) change their endings based on gender and case. Masculine nominative: mein Vater (no ending). Feminine/plural nominative: meine Mutter, meine Geschwister (add -e). Masculine accusative: meinen Vater (add -en).

Model: In meiner Familie gibt es meinen Vater, meine Mutter und meine Geschwister. Mein Bruder heißt Tom. Meine Eltern sind verheiratet. (In my family there is my father, my mother and my siblings. My brother is called Tom. My parents are married.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — family appears across all papers

gold.source_text: In my family there is my father, my mother, who is called Claudia, and my siblings. My parents are divorced.
model_answers: In meiner Familie gibt es meinen Vater, meine Mutter, die Claudia heißt, und meine Geschwister. Meine Eltern sind geschieden.

gold.question: Build the sentence in German

distractor_labels.der: wrong gender — Mutter is feminine, so the relative pronoun must be die, not der
distractor_labels.meinen: wrong case — Mutter is the subject (nominative), so use Meine, not meinen (accusative)
distractor_labels.heißen: wrong conjugation — the relative clause needs the er/sie form heißt, not the infinitive heißen

bullets.note: gibt es + accusative (meinen for masculine nouns)
bullets.prompt: Say how many people are in your family.
bullets.model_answer: In meiner Familie gibt es vier Personen: meinen Vater, meine Mutter, meinen Bruder und mich.

bullets.note: sein + adjectives with intensifiers (sehr, ein bisschen)
bullets.model_answer: Mein Bruder ist sehr witzig und ein bisschen frech.

bullets.note: relationship status vocab + reflexive verb sich verstehen
bullets.prompt: Say whether your parents are married or divorced.
bullets.model_answer: Meine Eltern sind verheiratet und sie verstehen sich gut.

bullets.note: relative clause: die (feminine) + verb heißt at end
bullets.prompt: Say you have a stepsister who is called Sophie.
bullets.model_answer: Ich habe eine Stiefschwester, die Sophie heißt.

bronze.question: Match the German family members to the English meaning
Match the German to the English meaning

wrong.mein: mein is the nominative form. After gibt es, you need the accusative: meinen for masculine nouns.
wrong.meine: meine is the feminine/plural form. Vater is masculine, so you need meinen.

gaps.correct_explain: meinen is correct because Vater is masculine and gibt es requires the accusative case.

wrong.mein: mein has no ending, which is only for masculine/neuter nominative. Mutter is feminine, so add -e.
wrong.meinen: meinen is the masculine accusative form. Mutter is feminine, so use meine.

gaps.correct_explain: meine is correct because Mutter is feminine. Feminine possessive adjectives stay the same in nominative and accusative.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence with the correct possessive adjective ending

gaps.correct_explain: verheiratet means married — the most common relationship status at GCSE.
Any name is acceptable here — the key structure is heißt + name.

bronze.question: Listen and type what you hear

wrong.heiße: heiße is the ich form. For meine Schwester (she), use heißt.
wrong.heißen: heißen is the infinitive or wir/sie (plural) form. Schwester is singular: heißt.

gaps.correct_explain: heißt is the er/sie/es form of heißen (to be called).

wrong.bin: bin is the ich form. The subject is sie (she): ist.
wrong.sind: sind is the plural form. Schwester is singular: ist.

gaps.correct_explain: ist is the er/sie/es form of sein (to be).

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Break the sentence at the conjunction und: 'Meine Schwester heißt Anna' + 'sie ist sehr lieb'.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Meine Schwester = my sister. heißt = is called. Anna = Anna.

steps.label: Answer

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Meine Schwester heißt Anna und sie ist sehr lieb.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Gibt es (there is/are) takes the accusative case because the family members are the direct object.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Vater is masculine (der Vater). In the accusative case, masculine possessive adjectives add -en.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Mein becomes meinen because Vater is masculine and follows gibt es (accusative). Feminine and neuter do not change: meine Mutter, mein Kind.
